title: Speonk (Neck, River, and Village)
summary: Speonk is a village in western Southampton, originally named for a neck of land, with Speonk River on the east.
history_content: The name appears in Southampton town records for meadow and upland at Speonk in 1712. The modern marker uses the present-day village area as a general reference for the older neck and river placename.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Speeunk, Speunk, Speonk, and Waspeunk. The name is interpreted as to the edge, margin, or border of a stream.

Why Place Names Matter

“Using Indigenous names instead of the English alternatives helps to reclaim Indigenous land stewardship, document Indigenous knowledge, and exhibits local Indigenous identity.”

— Dehrich A. Schmidt-Chya, Qikertarmiut Nunat Apertaarait Anirturluki: Preserving the Indigenous Place Names of the Kodiak Archipelago (2020), Abstract, PDF page iii
preservation_content: Speonk is a continuing Long Island placename where village, river, meadow, and neck names carry older Indigenous geography into modern maps.
